description: This bar chart illustrates five distinct patterns of parameter-efficient fine-tuning design spaces, each represented by a horizontal bar plot with five bars per group, labeled beneath the x-axis as “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck.” The horizontal axis represents the five categories, while the vertical axis, though unlabeled, represents the magnitude or value of the design space metric, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 1.0, as indicated by the tick marks at 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0. In the “Increasing” pattern, the bars rise in height from left to right, with approximate values of 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. The “Uniform” pattern shows all five bars at the same height of approximately 0.5. The “Decreasing” pattern shows bars falling in height from left to right, with approximate values of 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2, and 0.1. The “Spindle” pattern features two tall bars in the middle (approximately 0.6 and 0.6) flanked by two shorter bars (approximately 0.2 and 0.2) and a very short bar on the far left (approximately 0.1). The “Bottleneck” pattern has two tall bars on the left and right (approximately 0.6 and 0.6) with three shorter bars in the middle (approximately 0.2, 0.2, and 0.2). All bars are light green and are not sorted or emphasized in any particular way.
